disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, limits, and quotas are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.general: A valid South Dakota hunting or furbearer license is required (plus Habitat Stamp). River otter trapping is RESIDENTS ONLY with a furbearer license. Nonresidents may take only raccoon, beaver, and muskrat (Dec. 1, 2026–Mar. 15, 2027) and bobcats (Jan. 9–Feb. 15, 2027); mink and weasel may be trapped by nonresidents Dec. 1, 2026–Jan. 31, 2027. Raw furs may be kept after season close if checked with a GFP representative within 10 days.

species.notes: River otters are a CITES Appendix II species — SDGFP requires reporting, tagging, and carcass surrender. Nonresidents may not take otters (residents only).
permit_requirements: Limit of one river otter per resident hunter/trapper.
Statewide harvest limit of 30 — season ends prior to Dec. 31, 2026 if the harvest limit is reached.

Any harvested river otter must be reported to GFP within 24 hours of harvest. The entire carcass with the detached pelt must be submitted to GFP personnel within 5 days of capture. Once the season closes, an individual has 24 hours to notify a department representative of any untagged river otter harvested during the season. The pelt will be inspected, tagged, and registered; the tagged pelt is returned. The carcass is surrendered to GFP (may be returned upon request after biological data collection).
No person may possess, purchase, or sell raw river otter pelts that are not legally tagged.

verification.confirmation_notes: Data taken from the official 2026 South Dakota Hunting and Trapping Handbook (SDGFP): furbearer seasons table (p. 48), footnotes incl. nonresident windows, sunrise/sunset rule, otter limit 30/quota, bobcat bag limits (p. 49), bobcat/otter carcass registration and protected-animal list (pp. 50–52), and license table (p. 8).
